answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with deferred-withdrawal escrows. Every identity's earnings sit in a vault locked for fourteen epochs. Fraud proofs link identities sharing wallets or hardware; established peers judge them, and a guilty cluster's escrow goes to the reporter. An attacker running 500 fake identities must fund fourteen epochs of real compute to build $50 of locked earnings each, then risks losing all $25,000 to one proof. Dawn forges identities; the public atlas names every cluster caught. Sybils are gamblers leaving chips on the table while the house watches.
